about.title: Chino Hills Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Chino Hills is a city of about 78,000 people tucked against the western edge of San Bernardino County, and the products its residents rely on every day come from everywhere else. A car seat bought online, a space heater from a big-box store, a power tool, a medication, or a tire that separates on Carbon Canyon Road can each fail in ways nobody expected. When that failure causes an injury, California law does not make you prove the manufacturer was careless. Under strict liability, the questions are narrower: was the product defective in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and did that defect cause your harm? That framework matters here. In 2025, Chino Hills recorded 96 injury collisions and 131 people injured, and some crashes on SR-71 or Chino Hills Parkway trace back to a component that gave out rather than a driver's mistake. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect you, at no charge, with an independent attorney who handles defective-product claims and works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why Chino Hills Residents Use LawProactive for Defective-Product Claims

items.title: Strict Liability Changes the Question
items.desc: You generally do not need to show the maker was negligent; what matters is whether the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect that caused your injury. The attorneys we connect you with build cases around that standard.

items.title: Preserving the Product Comes First
items.desc: The broken heater, the failed tire, the cracked helmet is the evidence. We help you get to an attorney quickly so the item, packaging, and receipts are protected before anything is thrown away or returned.

items.title: More Than One Company May Be Responsible
items.desc: In California, manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all share liability for a defective product. An independent attorney can identify every party in that chain rather than stopping at the store where you bought it.

items.question: My tire failed on SR-71 near Chino Hills and I crashed. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It may be both, and the distinction matters. If the tire separated because of a manufacturing or design defect, the tire maker and possibly the seller can be strictly liable regardless of how you were driving. An attorney will want the tire itself preserved, along with maintenance records and photos from the scene, before any insurer disposes of the vehicle.

items.question: I already threw away the product that hurt me. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Losing the product makes a case harder, but it does not automatically end it. Receipts, photos, medical records, the product's model number, and recall notices can still help establish what you had and how it failed. Talk to an attorney before assuming the claim is gone.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive and hire the attorney?
items.answer: LawProactive charges you nothing; we are a free connection service, not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle product liability claims on contingency, meaning they are paid only if there is a recovery. If there is no recovery, you owe no attorney fee.
